skill.name: technical-writing
skill.description: Create clear technical documentation for specifications, architecture, runbooks, API references, user guides, release notes, and changelogs.
skill.summary: Create structured technical documentation for engineering and product teams.

content.value_statement: Teams lose time when technical docs are incomplete, inconsistent, or hard to scan. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code produce structured specs, runbooks, API docs, and architecture guides.
actual_capabilities: Selects structures for specs, architecture docs, runbooks, API docs, user guides, release notes, and changelogs.
Adapts tone and detail for developers, operations teams, stakeholders, and end users.
Provides templates with goals, design details, testing strategy, rollout plans, and open questions.
Recommends examples, tables, diagrams, screenshots, and checklists for clearer documentation.
Applies review guidance for clarity, consistency, maintenance, and audience fit.
limitations: Does not verify whether sample commands or API details are correct for your system.
Needs source material from the user to produce accurate project-specific documentation.
Cannot replace review by engineers, security owners, or product stakeholders.
Does not generate diagrams from live infrastructure without supplied architecture details.

use_cases.title: Draft Feature Specs
use_cases.description: Turn feature notes into a technical specification with goals, design details, testing, rollout, and open questions.

use_cases.title: Build Incident Runbooks
use_cases.description: Create operational guides that document dependencies, monitoring signals, recovery steps, and escalation paths.

use_cases.title: Prepare API Documentation
use_cases.description: Organize endpoint behavior, authentication, parameters, examples, and error responses for developer readers.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Spec
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a first structured draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a beginner-friendly technical spec for [feature]. Use these notes: [notes]. Include goals, non-goals, design, testing, rollout, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request to refine existing documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this draft for developers and operations teams: [draft]. Improve structure, define terms, add missing prerequisites, and flag unclear areas.

prompt_templates.title: Document Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a system design document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an architecture document for [system]. Include components, data flow, key decisions, scalability, security, monitoring, disaster recovery, and future considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Documentation Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request to find gaps across existing docs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this documentation set: [links or text]. Identify gaps, outdated sections, missing examples, unclear ownership, and a maintenance plan.

output_examples.input: Notes for a payment retry feature with rollout concerns and unanswered edge cases.
output_examples.output: A feature spec outline with overview, problem statement, goals, design approach, test plan, rollout plan, rollback plan, and open questions.

output_examples.input: A short service runbook that lacks troubleshooting and escalation details.
output_examples.output: A revised runbook with service overview, dependencies, deployment steps, monitoring checks, common incidents, escalation paths, and maintenance notes.

output_examples.input: A list of API endpoints with authentication notes and expected errors.
output_examples.output: An API documentation draft with authentication guidance, endpoint summaries, parameter tables, request descriptions, error responses, and version notes.

best_practices: Provide source notes, audience, and document type before asking for a draft.
Ask the model to flag assumptions and open questions instead of filling unknown details.
Have the target audience test instructions before publishing important documentation.
anti_patterns: Requesting a complete runbook without service details, owners, alerts, or recovery steps.
Publishing generated API documentation without checking endpoints, permissions, examples, and error behavior.
Using one document for developers, operators, and executives without adjusting detail.

faq.question: What documents can this skill help create?
faq.answer: It supports technical specs, architecture docs, runbooks, API docs, user guides, release notes, and changelogs.

faq.question: Does it run the sample commands it writes?
faq.answer: No. It writes documentation examples only. Users must test commands in their own environment.

faq.question: Can it write for non-technical readers?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes audience guidance for stakeholders and end users with simpler language.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the audience, document goal, system context, source notes, constraints, and known open questions.

faq.question: Can it review existing documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify unclear sections, missing prerequisites, outdated details, weak examples, and maintenance gaps.

faq.question: Is this suitable for Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill uses reading and editing tools, so it can support Claude, Claude Code, and Codex workflows.
